notes:
POC focused on Dedicated capacity + SLA negotiation. Customer is a payments platform building conversational agent for merchant support and realtime reranking for fraud signals. Primary asks: hard throughput guarantees, deterministic p99 latency SLOs, reserved GPU planning (no surprise bursts), and strict audit/KMS controls.

Key constraints / paraphrases from customer: "we need p99 < 200ms for chat at 50 req/s sustained with 4k context" — they repeated the requirement for deterministic tail latencies. High sensitivity to interruptions: warm-KV cache behavior, cold-start penalties are unacceptable for certain flows.

POC summary so far: ran a 6h load run against a dedicated small pool (4x A100 equiv) using quantized 34B model. Test harness: 2500 sample prompts (mix of short chat, long context summarization, and reranking queries). Observed metrics: median latency ~72ms, p90 ~105ms, p99 ~235ms under 75% CPU/GPU utilization; throughput flattened at bursts >85% and we saw KV eviction during large-batch bursts.

Next POC steps we've agreed: - 48h soak with warmed KV vs cold-KV windows (24h warm, 12h cold cycles) - Autoscale + reserved capacity validation: test scaling from 4->8->12 GPU equivalent with controlled traffic to validate routing/fallback latency delta - Fault-injection: network jitter and model fallback to smaller variant for graceful degradation - SLA language workshop: team to propose measurable SLO metrics (p50/p90/p99, error budget, MTTR) and penalty/remediation matrix.

Stakeholder notes: Eng lead (Marcus Chen) cares most about p99 determinism. Security lead (Lina Ortega) wants KMS integration and proof of audit logs for every inference. Procurement pushed back on long-term reservation until we demonstrate linear cost/throughput gains in soak tests.

Open items: confirm HSM/KMS integration timeline, provide final GPU reservation quote (8 vs 12 H100 equiv), clarify fallback model latency delta, legal to propose SLA redlines back by 2026-03-12.
